clue.text: Performed around the edge and went separate ways

indicators.note: the word for performed wraps around the word for the edge

parts.note: performed means did, as in 'did a dance'
a verge is an edge or border, as of a road

explanation.surface: Someone performed on the fringes before the group split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths or people that diverge part and head off in different directions.

clue.text: Tenor is excited about performing rock

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit about, that is around, the word for performing
excited suggests the letters of the two words are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: a performer who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: An opera tenor is thrilled to be on stage singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' and 'performing' read as a singer on stage; 'excited' makes IRSTONE, which 'about' wraps around the stage word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron ore.

clue.text: Hospital to manage with revolutionary procedure for a time

indicators.note: a revolutionary procedure turns things over, so the combined letters are read from the end back

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to cope is to manage or get by

explanation.surface: A hospital tries out a groundbreaking operation for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with revolutionary procedure' turns H + COPE round to give EPOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period or era in history.

clue.text: Marge's not so terribly special for them?

definitions.text: Marge's not so terribly special for them?

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled into a new arrangement

parts.note: the name or the spread, with its S kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Food lovers would not think much of margarine as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles MARGES NOT SO into the answer; the whole clue also describes it, since marge (margarine) is no delicacy to discerning eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomes are gourmets, connoisseurs of fine food who would scorn cheap spread.

clue.text: Composer ruminates, losing speed

indicators.note: losing means the word for speed is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to ruminate is to ponder or deliberate
rate means speed, as in 'at a fast rate'

explanation.surface: A composer slowly mulls things over.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking RATE out of DELIBERATES leaves DELIBES. Léo Delibes was a French composer of ballets such as Coppélia.
explanation.definitionFit: Delibes was a nineteenth-century French composer, known for Lakmé and Coppélia.

clue.text: Ornaments provided by church members

parts.note: arms are limbs, and limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Decorations donated by the congregation of a parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Charms are small trinkets worn on a bracelet or chain as decoration.

clue.text: Sound sophisticated, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: cool can mean stylish and sophisticated

explanation.surface: Seeming nearly refined.
explanation.definitionFit: A coo is the soft murmuring call of a dove or pigeon.

clue.text: Artist is entertained by a quiet friend offering assessment

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pal is a friend
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is hosted by a quiet friend who gives an opinion of the work.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; 'entertained by' means taken inside, as a guest is.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an evaluation or judgement of worth.

clue.text: Fellow joining diocese shortly to be presented with minister's home

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A man joins the diocese and is soon given a house for the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in Scottish churches.

clue.text: Bog drowning black wolf

indicators.note: something drowning is submerged, so the letter for black goes inside the word for bog

parts.note: bog and loo are both slang for a toilet
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark creature sinks in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' looks like a swamp, but it is the slang toilet, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobo is a grey wolf of the American Southwest; the word is Spanish for wolf.

clue.text: Colour of edible seed that's chopped, soft, put in basin

indicators.note: put in means the trimmed seed and the soft letter go inside the word for basin

parts.note: a sink is a basin

indicators.note: chopped means cut off at the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: an almond is an edible seed or nut
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: chop a nut, soften it and put it in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a recipe step; 'that's chopped' docks the nut's tail to ALMON, and 'put in' places that and the soft letter in the basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon pink is the orange-pink shade of the fish's flesh.

clue.text: Characters saved by bravest hero in book

indicators.note: characters are letters, and those saved by the following words are kept inside them

explanation.surface: Characters rescued by a valiant hero in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters saved by' points to letters running across 'bravest hero'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament telling of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Fighting groups based abroad collecting equipment

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the scrambled letters surround the word for equipment
abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: rig means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Army units stationed overseas gather kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' here means scattered rather than overseas, making BADES, which 'collecting' wraps around the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigades are military formations of several battalions.

clue.text: Like ship over the Mariana trench experiencing difficulty

definitions.text: Like ship over the Mariana trench

explanation.surface: A ship above the ocean's deepest point is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mariana Trench is the ocean's deepest point, so a ship above it floats on very deep sea; the idiom also means being in serious trouble.

clue.text: Way the navy is presented by journalist as being up to date

parts.note: a mode is a way or method
RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter explains how the navy is keeping up with the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modernised has been brought into line with current ways.

clue.text: Advance around home in serious manner

indicators.note: around means the word for advance goes around the word for home

parts.note: advance as an adjective means early, as in advance warning
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Moving forward around the house with a solemn air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective, as in 'advance booking', meaning EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act earnestly is to act sincerely and seriously.

clue.text: Cashier's bag

explanation.surface: A bank teller's carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier someone is to dismiss them, especially from the armed forces; a sack is also a large bag.

clue.text: Cannot a bad temper get conveyed by singing style?

parts.note: cannot contracts to can't
bile means bad temper or irritability

explanation.surface: Can an angry mood be expressed through song?
explanation.definitionFit: Cantabile is a musical direction meaning in a smooth, flowing, songlike way.

clue.text: Something that may be seen across river, peculiar, lacking tail

definitions.text: Something that may be seen across river

indicators.note: lacking a tail means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: weird means peculiar or strange

explanation.surface: An odd tailless thing spotted across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam built across a river to control its flow.

clue.text: Is room transversed by many a motley group?

indicators.note: being crossed through by a word means sitting inside it, so these letters go within the word for many

parts.note: taken as written
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A question about whether a crowd crossing a room makes an odd gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transversed' (crossed through) is an unusual container signal: the room is inside the crowd, not the crowd inside the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed assortment or collection of varied items.

clue.text: Meals for each with drinks all round

indicators.note: all round means the word for drinks surrounds the word for each

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Dinners for everyone with a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppers are evening meals.

clue.text: Wayward sheep cur rallies

indicators.note: wayward means unruly or straying, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved sheepdog livens things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally someone is to lift their spirits, to make them happier.

clue.text: As a result, barrier will need new coping

indicators.note: coping is the top course of a wall, so in this down entry the top letter is replaced

parts.note: a fence is a barrier

explanation.surface: A wall-builder says the barrier must get a fresh top layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will need new coping' swaps the top letter of FENCE, which stands first in this down light; the clue does not say which letter goes in, so the definition settles it as H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence means therefore, for this reason.

clue.text: Funny guy not completely healthy, nevertheless

parts.note: a wit is a funny, clever person

indicators.note: not completely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A comedian who is not entirely well, all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Withal is an old word for moreover or notwithstanding.

clue.text: Vehicle has minimal power? Walk!

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
P, the abbreviation for power, is the smallest form of the word

explanation.surface: The bus is underpowered, so go on foot!
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trek a long way.

clue.text: Legal document giving order not about to restrict men

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the shortened word encloses the men
not means the letter for about is left out of the word

parts.note: to instruct is to order
C stands for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deed issuing a command that men's movements be limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving order' reads as a court ruling; 'not' takes the circa letter out to leave INSTRUT, and 'to restrict' has it enclose the men.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an instrument is a formal document such as a deed or contract.

clue.text: Vessel to go round in circles, losing time

indicators.note: losing means the letter for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: to turn is to rotate, go round

explanation.surface: A ship spinning helplessly and wasting time.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, often for ashes.

clue.text: Keen man heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter, the head, is removed

parts.note: David is a man's name

explanation.surface: An eager fellow setting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: African with range of knowledge: no going back

parts.note: ken is the range of one's knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

indicators.note: going back means the word for no is read in reverse

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A well-informed African who will not retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya in East Africa.

clue.text: Fighter more disjointed, one knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: scrappier means more fragmentary and disjointed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boxer becomes less coordinated after one is floored.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapper is someone who loves a fight, a brawler.
